speaker: Sunshine
text: [excitedly] Character number two is "Bù." Fourth tone, the falling one. It means "not," or just "no." This is the super important part: it's the other half of yes and no.

speaker: Rob
text: This used to be my daughter's favorite word. It still is, but it used to be, too. [dryly] So we learned yes, and now we're learning no. Seems like a very balanced show, we're making here.

speaker: Sunshine
text: [laughs] Exactly. Put the two together and you can ask real questions and answer them. But first, let's look at it.

speaker: Rob
text: [thoughtfully] Okay. There's a flat line across the top and a stroke dropping down from the middle. Then two little strokes kick out underneath, one left, one right. It looks like a tiny tree. Or a coat rack.

speaker: Sunshine
text: A tree is good! Some people see a bird with its wings spread out. Here's a memory trick. Imagine a bird flying up and hitting something flat above it, like a ceiling. It can't get through. So: no. Not.

speaker: Rob
text: Denied, rejected, no way José. I can remember that.

speaker: Sunshine
text: Good. "Bù" works on its own. If someone asks you something, you can just answer "Bù." No. Or you put it in front of another word to make that word negative.
